info.title: Global Speko Relay streaming API
info.description: WebSocket contract of the Global Speko Relay: streaming speech-to-text and text-to-speech sessions. JSON text frames carry the control messages and events documented here; binary frames carry raw audio in the format the session.configure frame declared, with no JSON envelope. The Go types in package relayapi are the source of truth for every shape in this document, and speccheck_test.go machine-checks the two against each other. The HTTP endpoints are specified separately in openapi.yaml.

relay.description: Global entry point. The upgrade request authenticates with a Speko-issued bearer token and must carry an Idempotency-Key header. The idempotency content hash of a WebSocket session is the SHA-256 of the exact session.configure text-frame bytes, so a retry must reproduce the configure frame byte-for-byte; later frames are intentionally outside the hash — they are the stream's continuous content, guarded by budgets and leases, while the configure frame is the session's intent.

/v1/stt/stream.description: Streaming speech-to-text. The first text frame MUST be session.configure; its exact frame bytes are the session's idempotency content hash. Audio input travels in binary frames in the format the configure frame declared, and the client must not send audio before session.ready arrives. Exactly one terminal frame — session.closed or error — ends every session.

Idempotency-Key.description: Required on the upgrade request. The relay persists only the key, a content hash, and the session's execution status — never the content itself. The hash covers the exact session.configure text-frame bytes; later frames are intentionally outside the hash. Reusing a key with the same hash while the original admission is still live returns request_in_progress (retryable); after dispatch it returns request_already_started with the original request id; reusing a key with a different hash returns idempotency_conflict. Keys are opaque, and the normative length bound is 256 BYTES — maxLength below counts code points, which JSON Schema cannot avoid, so multi-byte keys hit the byte bound first.

publish.description: JSON control frames, plus untyped binary frames carrying audio input.

subscribe.description: session.ready is always the first event frame; exactly one terminal frame — session.closed or error — ends the session.

/v1/tts/stream.description: Streaming text-to-speech. The first text frame MUST be session.configure; its exact frame bytes are the session's idempotency content hash. The client must not append text before session.ready arrives. Synthesized audio travels in binary frames between the utterance.started and utterance.done events that share its sequence number. Exactly one terminal frame — session.closed or error — ends every session.

Idempotency-Key.description: Required on the upgrade request. The relay persists only the key, a content hash, and the session's execution status — never the content itself. The hash covers the exact session.configure text-frame bytes; later frames are intentionally outside the hash. Reusing a key with the same hash while the original admission is still live returns request_in_progress (retryable); after dispatch it returns request_already_started with the original request id; reusing a key with a different hash returns idempotency_conflict. Keys are opaque, and the normative length bound is 256 BYTES — maxLength below counts code points, which JSON Schema cannot avoid, so multi-byte keys hit the byte bound first.

bearerAuth.description: Speko-issued API credential presented as a bearer token on the upgrade request. Failures normalize to the authentication_failed error code.

wsError.name: error
wsError.title: Terminal error frame
wsError.summary: The terminal error frame, shared by STT and TTS sessions. The type name matches the SSE error event deliberately: one error vocabulary across every streaming transport.

RoutingMode.description: Discriminates the routing tagged union. The set is closed: an empty or unknown mode is rejected so a typo can never silently fall back to automatic provider selection.

RoutingObjective.description: Ranks auto-mode candidates. Unknown objectives are rejected rather than treated as balanced so callers learn about typos before any money is reserved.

Routing.description:
Selects how the relay picks a provider for one session. It is a tagged union over mode: auto carries the objective and optional allow/deny provider filters, explicit carries exactly a provider and model. Fields from the other arm are rejected in both directions; a present-but-empty filter array ([]) counts as present and is rejected in explicit mode, while an empty-string provider or model in auto mode is indistinguishable from omission and tolerated as such. A wholly omitted routing object means {mode: auto, objective: balanced}, and an auto routing without an objective defaults to balanced — the default exists for omission, never for partially specified routing.
Explicit mode also accepts the combined "provider/model" spelling in the model field: {"model": "openai/gpt-5.2"} with no provider splits at the first slash, and a model redundantly prefixed with the stated provider has the prefix stripped. Upstream model ids that themselves contain a slash must therefore name the provider one way or the other, e.g. "together/meta-llama/Llama-X" or provider "together" with model "meta-llama/Llama-X".

allow_providers.description: Auto mode only. Provider ids must not be blank.

deny_providers.description: Auto mode only. Provider ids must not be blank.

provider.description: Explicit mode only, and required there.

model.description: Explicit mode only, and required there. Accepts either the bare model id with the provider field set, or the combined "provider/model" form with the provider field omitted.

Route.description: The response-side counterpart of Routing: the concrete decision that served a session. region is the Speko relay location, not a provider-processing residency guarantee, and attempt_id identifies the (possibly post-fallback) attempt that produced the output.

AudioConfig.description: Raw audio on a relay stream: the binary input frames of an STT session, or the synthesized output frames of a TTS session. The bounds match the local gateway's portable media contract so a caller can move between provider-direct and relay routes without re-encoding.

Usage.description: Normalized, provider-neutral quantities for one session. Only the lines relevant to the session's kind are set; zero lines are omitted on the wire. Split lines are mutually exclusive by contract: a token counted in cached_input_tokens is not repeated in input_tokens, and a reasoning token is not repeated in output_tokens, so the splits always sum to the totals.

TranscriptSegment.description: One time-aligned span of the transcript.

speaker.description: Whoever said the span, present only when the request asked for diarization and the provider attributed it. The VENDOR's own label carried verbatim ("A" from one provider, "1" from another): renumbering across providers would invent an identity mapping no vendor promised. Absent means unattributed, which is not the same as a new speaker.

ErrorCode.description: Stable, machine-readable failure class. The set is closed: the relay normalizes every failure — including provider failures — to one of these codes and never forwards a raw provider response body. On an established WebSocket session the code arrives in a terminal error frame and no HTTP status applies; when the same code is returned over HTTP — including a rejected upgrade — it maps to one canonical status: 400 capability_unsupported and invalid_request; 401 authentication_failed; 402 insufficient_credit; 409 idempotency_conflict, request_in_progress, and request_already_started; 413 payload_too_large; 415 unsupported_media; 429 rate_limited and concurrency_exhausted; 500 relay_error; 502 provider_error; 503 provider_unavailable.

ErrorBody.description: The normalized failure detail. message is human-readable and intentionally carries no provider payload; request_id is present whenever a relay request id had been minted before the failure.

ErrorEvent.description: The terminal error frame on a WebSocket session. Exactly one terminal frame — session.closed or error — ends every session.

STTSessionConfigure.description: Opens a streaming transcription. audio describes the raw binary frames the client will send: streamed audio has no container, so the format must be declared up front. The exact frame bytes are the session's idempotency content hash; later frames are intentionally outside the hash.

routing.description: Omitted entirely, routing means {mode: auto, objective: balanced}.

options.description: Transcription feature asks and per-provider settings for the whole session. They ride this frame — and therefore the session's idempotency hash — because they are session intent, not stream content: later frames cannot change them.

STTOptions.description: What a caller asked a transcription to do beyond returning text. The same object rides POST /v1/stt/transcriptions and the STT session.configure frame, in the same vocabulary the local gateway uses. The canonical asks (diarization, keywords, noise_reduction) fail closed: a session whose routed model does not advertise the matching capability in GET /v1/models is rejected with capability_unsupported, never answered with the feature quietly missing. Names arrive lower case and are rejected otherwise rather than folded, because the idempotency content hash covers the configure frame bytes exactly as sent and one intent must have one spelling.

diarization.description: Label each transcript segment with the speaker who said it. Omitted leaves the vendor default, which is not the same as false.

keywords.description: Vocabulary-biasing terms (names, products, jargon), translated to each vendor's own spelling. At most 100 terms of at most 64 characters each; both bounds count CHARACTERS, which JSON Schema cannot express, so they are normative here in prose and enforced by the relay.

noise_reduction.description: Ask the provider to clean the audio before transcribing.

provider_options.description: The vendor's OWN settings, namespaced by provider name, e.g. {"deepgram": {"numerals": true}}. Values are scalars only (boolean, number, or string of at most 256 characters). At most 8 providers, each with at most 16 settings. Settings addressed to a provider the session does not reach are ignored by design, so they never narrow routing. The relay forwards only the keys the routed provider allow-lists and refuses the rest by name; keys it owns itself (model, language, encoding, sample_rate, credentials, and the canonical asks' own vendor spellings) are always refused.

STTInputCommit.description: Marks the end of the audio the client wants finalized.

STTSessionClose.description: Asks the server to finish outstanding transcripts and end the session with a terminal session.closed frame.

STTSessionReady.description: Confirms admission and reports the concrete route. It is always the first event frame; the client must not send audio before it.

STTTranscriptDelta.description: An interim hypothesis; later deltas and the next transcript.final supersede it. Deltas are never empty — empty interim hypotheses are dropped at normalization, never forwarded.

STTTranscriptFinal.description: A finalized span of transcript with optional time-aligned segments. text may be empty: a finalized span of silence is legitimate.

speaker.description: Whoever said the whole finalized span, present only when the session asked for diarization and the provider attributed the turn. Most providers report one speaker per finalized turn rather than per span, so this is where a diarized session usually reads its labels; per-span attribution rides segments[].speaker instead. The vendor's own label, verbatim.

STTUsageUpdated.description: Cumulative usage while the stream is live, so callers can watch spend before the terminal frame.

STTSessionClosed.description: The clean terminal frame carrying final usage.

TTSSessionConfigure.description: Opens a streaming synthesis session. audio is the requested output format of the binary frames the server will send. The exact frame bytes are the session's idempotency content hash; later frames are intentionally outside the hash. The frame carries no language field yet; the relay currently synthesizes English.

routing.description: Omitted entirely, routing means {mode: auto, objective: balanced}.

voice.description: Optional: in auto mode the party that picks the provider picks a default voice for it.

TTSInputAppend.description: Adds text to the utterance being assembled. Characters are counted against the reserved budget when appended, so an over-budget append fails before any provider work happens.

TTSInputCommit.description: Finalizes the appended text as one utterance and starts synthesis.

TTSInputCancel.description: Abandons uncommitted appended text and any in-flight synthesis for the current utterance.

TTSSessionClose.description: Asks the server to finish outstanding synthesis and end the session with a terminal session.closed frame.

TTSSessionReady.description: Confirms admission and reports the concrete route. It is always the first event frame; the client must not append text before it.

TTSUtteranceStarted.description: Announces the binary audio frames for one committed utterance. sequence is the 1-based utterance index within the session so clients can correlate audio with commits.

TTSUtteranceDone.description: Marks the end of one utterance's binary audio frames.

TTSUsageUpdated.description: Cumulative usage while the stream is live, so callers can watch spend before the terminal frame.

TTSSessionClosed.description: The clean terminal frame carrying final usage.
